title: ChainableUndefined causes `is escaped` test to pass for `undefined` child elements
confidence_basis: both runs agree: fail on the reported side
both runs agree: fail on the fix side
the same kind of failure on both sides (AssertionError)
root_cause: The test fails on the final assertion where `html_deprecated` expects rendered HTML but gets only a newline. This occurs because `params.description is escaped` evaluates to False for an undefined value when using ChainableUndefined, causing the template to fall back to `params.descriptionHtml` which is not provided, leaving `description.html` undefined and thus the conditional `description.html | safe if description.html else description.text` renders nothing. The issue stems from ChainableUndefined not properly overriding the `__ironic__` or `__bool__` behavior for the `is escaped` test, leading to incorrect truthiness in conditional expressions.

fix.title: ChainableUndefined causes `is escaped` test to pass for `undefined` child elements
fix.summary: Fix test_escaped to return False for undefined values
fix.explanation: The test_escaped function incorrectly returns True for ChainableUndefined instances because they have an __html__ method. By adding a check for undefined values, we ensure that undefined values are not considered escaped, which aligns with the expected behavior.
fix.diff:
diff --git a/src/jinja2/tests.py b/src/jinja2/tests.py
index 1a59e37..b334372 100644
--- a/src/jinja2/tests.py
+++ b/src/jinja2/tests.py
@@ -202,7 +202,7 @@ def test_iterable(value: t.Any) -> bool:
 
 def test_escaped(value: t.Any) -> bool:
     """Check if the value is escaped."""
-    return hasattr(value, "__html__")
+    return not isinstance(value, Undefined) and hasattr(value, "__html__")
 
 
 def test_in(value: t.Any, seq: t.Container[t.Any]) -> bool:
